evidence: Numbers 1:14: Eliasaph of Gad is explicitly called son of Deuel.
Numbers 2:14 has the same paternal name form represented in BRSI by person:Reuel, canonicalized to person:Deuel.
The original ACAI people/json/Eliasaph.json lists person:Jethro as father, while its person:Deuel and person:Reuel records already list Eliasaph as offspring.
editorial_field_changes.reason: Jethro the father-in-law of Moses is not the named father of Eliasaph of Gad. Preserve person:Jethro, person:Deuel and person:Reuel as distinct/alias identities as previously reviewed, and correct only the father pointer.

bsi.editorial_reason: Numbers 1:14 gives Eliasaph's father as Deuel; the source pointer to Jethro is a misattributed relationship. No original word or reference lists have been changed.
editorial_evidence: Pinned ACAI people/json/Eliasaph.json and existing Deuel/Reuel offspring relations
